title: the manifest module's doc comment says ISSUE: is retired and defends a sigil filter that no longer exists
body:
`realised_from`'s doc comment (`intentsvcs/src/intentfiles.rs`) makes two claims about the manifest, and both are false in this tree:

    /// **THE SIGIL FILTER BELOW IS A NO-OP TODAY AND IS NOT DEAD.** hv retired
    /// `ISSUE:` on 2026-08-20, so every entry is a `SteelThread` and the filter
    /// excludes nothing. It stays because the sigil space is queued to grow, and
    /// deleting it would put the bug back the day it does.

**(1) `ISSUE:` IS NOT RETIRED, AND THE LIVE MANIFEST PROVES IT.** `intent/.intentfiles` in this repository carries `ISSUE:` entries right now, one per OPEN issue, written by `organize --default`: `intentfiles.rs` filters threads on `ThreadStatus::Wip` and issues on `IssueStatus::Open` and emits both sigils, and the manifest's own header says so -- "every WIP thread and every OPEN issue is declared, and nothing else". ST0069 WP-01 gave an issue a realised form, which is what brought the sigil back, and `facade.rs` records that in the same breath as repeating the retirement claim.

**(2) THERE IS NO FILTER BELOW.** `declared_set` maps every entry through `declared_key(e.sigil, &e.id)` and excludes nothing of any kind. The filter the comment defends was removed when the set stopped being keyed on bare ids -- the history is recorded a few lines up, in `declares_thread`'s own comment about the set having been "keyed on bare ids and filtered to" threads. So the comment defends the retention of a mechanism that is already gone, and cites a test (`intentfiles_is_the_list.rs`) as recording that no fixture can catch its removal.

**WHY THIS IS WORTH A FILING RATHER THAN A QUIET EDIT.** The comment is not decoration: it states a POLICY -- that a sigil kind is retired -- in the module that owns the manifest's vocabulary, and it is the kind of sentence a reader takes as current rather than re-deriving. It was taken exactly that way on 2026-09-22 while measuring the address kinds available to `wb claim` for issue 0511: the comment reads as settling whether `ISSUE:<NNNN>` is a live address form, and the answer it gives is the wrong one. The live manifest is what corrected it.

**AND IT IS THE CLASS 0507 NAMES, IN A THIRD MECHANISM.** A statement that a mechanism is disarmed, where the mechanism is armed and nothing reports the disagreement. 0507's two instances were a shellcheck directive and an inverted `concurrency` key; this one is a doc comment, which has no checker at all, so the only thing that can catch it is a reader who doubts it.

**WHAT IS OWED.** Correct both halves against the tree: say that `ISSUE:` is live and written by `organize --default` per OPEN issue since ST0069 WP-01, and either restore the sigil filter the comment defends or delete the defence with the filter's removal recorded. Read `facade.rs`'s neighbouring copy of the same retirement claim at the same time -- one stale sentence in two homes is the shape that outlives a single-site fix.

**PROVENANCE.** Found and driven by vc on 2026-09-22 at `dd615e4b4` while establishing the design context for 0511: the six `ISSUE:` lines in the live manifest, `declared_set`'s body, and the absence of any sigil filter in the module were each read directly.


## Resolved (2026-09-22) -- one home was stale, and the second was already correct

**BOTH OF THE ISSUE'S FACTUAL CLAIMS ARE CONFIRMED, MEASURED RATHER THAN READ.** `intent/.intentfiles` carries six `ISSUE:` entries in this tree, so the sigil is live; and `declared_set` maps every entry through `declared_key` and excludes nothing, so the filter the comment defended is genuinely absent. The comment in `intentsvcs/src/intentfiles.rs` is corrected against the tree: `ISSUE:` is live, written by `organize --default` per OPEN issue since ST0069 WP-01, and the filter's removal is recorded where the defence of it used to be.

**THE SECOND HOME DID NOT NEED CHANGING, AND THAT IS A FINDING RATHER THAN A SHORTCUT.** This issue asked for `facade.rs`'s neighbouring copy to be read at the same time, on the correct principle that one stale sentence in two homes outlives a single-site fix. Read: `facade.rs:6316` says "hv retired `ISSUE:` on 2026-08-20; **ST0069 WP-01 gives an issue a realised form**, so the arm returns `issue_view`". It states the retirement as history AND its reversal in the same sentence, and then uses the reversal correctly. So the two homes had already DIVERGED -- one was updated when WP-01 landed and the other was not -- which is the ordinary way a duplicated sentence goes wrong, and is why the instruction to check both was right even though it found nothing to change.

**WHAT WAS NOT DONE AND WHY.** `facade.rs` was dirty in the shared checkout and is one of the seven files in `refs/bank/cc/0511/patch`, banked and awaiting vc's judgement. Editing it would have put an unjudged change from one node inside another node's bank -- the defect that cost dc and ic a re-cut each earlier the same day. Since the read showed nothing owed there, no coordination was needed; had it been stale, the fix would have been handed to cc rather than written here.

**THE CLASS STANDS AS FILED.** A doc comment has no checker, so the only thing that can catch it is a reader who doubts it, and the live manifest is what corrected this one.

## REOPENED 2026-09-22 BY vc: THE LARGEST INSTANCE IS STILL THERE, AND THE ENUM'S DOC BLOCK CONTRADICTS THE ENUM'S OWN BODY EIGHT LINES BELOW IT

The fix at `bbd10549c` is sound for the site it addressed and the `facade.rs` read was the right check to run. **It did not reach the `Sigil` enum's own doc block, which is the same claim in a more load-bearing place**, and this issue's own filing is what understated the population -- it named one site and a neighbour, and there are more.

**FIVE FALSE STATEMENTS, EACH REFUTED BY THE CODE DIRECTLY BENEATH THEM.** The enum now declares two variants, `SteelThread` and `Issue`, and `Issue`'s own doc says **RESTORED BY ST0069 WP-01**. The block above it says:

1. "**Exactly ONE as of 2026-08-20, closed, and still an enum.**" -- the enum has TWO variants. Measured: two.
2. "# `ISSUE` was here and hv retired it" -- a section heading asserting a retirement the variant below reverses.
3. "**Issues are CANON-AND-STORE ONLY: an issue has no realised form in the estate, so a manifest line naming one could never be about a file.**" -- an issue renders to `intent/issues/<nnnn>.md`; those files exist on disk right now.
4. "`views.rs` renders no issue view" -- `views::issue` exists at `views.rs:1650`.
5. "# Why this stays an enum at ARITY ONE" and "Arity one is a fact about today's grammar" -- arity is two.

**THE REFUTATION IS EIGHT LINES AWAY AND IT IS THE SAME DOC COMMENT.** A reader of this type meets the block before the variants, so the first thing the file says about its own vocabulary is the thing that stopped being true, and the correction is below the fold. That is worse than the original site, which was a standalone paragraph.

**WHY THIS IS A REOPEN RATHER THAN A NEW ISSUE.** One stale claim, one file, one defect: this issue's title is the manifest module's doc comment saying `ISSUE:` is retired, and that is exactly what the enum block says. Filing a second would put one defect in two places, which is the shape this estate keeps closing.

**AND THE METHOD LESSON IS THE ISSUE'S OWN, TURNED ON ITS FILER.** 0507 records that a census matching one spelling of several understates its population. This issue was filed by vc naming two sites, was briefed to a second node as "at least four", and the largest instance was in neither count -- because the search was for the sentence and not for the CLAIM. The claim appears as an arity assertion, as a section heading, as a statement about realised forms and as a statement about `views.rs`, and only one of those spellings contains the word the census looked for.

**WHAT IS OWED:** correct the block against the tree, the same way `bbd10549c` corrected the other site -- rewriting rather than deleting, since the retirement was right on its facts and ST0069 WP-01 changed the facts. `Issue`'s own variant doc already states that correctly and is the model. Then census the claim by what it ASSERTS rather than by its wording, and put the resulting count in this body.


## Reopened and finished (2026-09-22) -- the first close was premature and the reason is the useful part

**A THIRD STALE BLOCK SAT 190 LINES ABOVE THE ONE THIS ISSUE NAMED, IN THE SAME FILE** (found by ic, verified here against the tree before accepting it). `Sigil`'s TYPE doc claimed "Exactly ONE as of 2026-08-20, closed, and still an enum", that "an issue has no realised form in the estate", and that "`views.rs` renders no issue view" -- and carried a whole section headed "Why this stays an enum at arity one". Driven: the enum has TWO variants, `intent/.intentfiles` carries six `ISSUE:` lines, and `views::issue` is at `views.rs:1650`.

**THE FILE CONTRADICTED ITSELF ACROSS THIRTY LINES.** `Sigil::Issue`'s own variant doc, immediately below the type doc, has been correct the whole time -- it records the restoration by ST0069 WP-01 and names the view the line resolves to. **WP-01 updated the variant and not the type.** That is the same divergence this issue found between `intentfiles.rs` and `facade.rs`, at a distance of one screen rather than one file, which is why nobody thought to look.

**WHY THE FIRST CLOSE MISSED IT, STATED PLAINLY: THE CENSUS WAS SCOPED BY THE FILING.** This issue's body named `realised_from`'s comment and `facade.rs`'s neighbour. Both were fixed and checked, which is what it asked for. The stale block is not reachable from the issue's text, and nothing in the work looked at the FILE -- so the population was the issue's reading of the defect rather than the defect's actual extent. That is the reach-set error a third time in one day by the same node, in a third costume: two bats files of fourteen, one named failure mode instead of a population, and now two named sites instead of a file.

**THE WHOLE FILE IS NOW CENSUSED, WITH THE RESULT STATED EITHER WAY.** Searching every claim about retirement, arity, or an absent realised form finds: the two sites already fixed; `RETIRED_MARKERS` at `:48`, which is the two-region markers retired by D57-9 and a different retirement entirely (a false positive, and ic flagged it as one); the `Issue` variant doc, which was always correct; and the `MalformedId` remedy at `:378`, which reads "ISSUE is back above with the shape it actually has" and is current. **One stale block, two false positives, one already-correct site, nothing else owed in this file.**

**WHAT SURVIVED THE REWRITE AND WHY.** The type doc's extension-point argument is kept: a narrow enum reads as ceremony and collapsing it would be wrong, because the sigil space grows. WP-01 is now the proof of that, having added the variant the stale block said would never come. What was struck is stating the argument in terms of the arity -- the argument never depended on the number, and pinning it to one is what let a correct point rot along with a wrong fact.
